uncertainties.note: Jouhou-bu rendered as 'Intelligence' (department). No locked term exists; Eureka Seven wiki calls Dominic an intelligence officer. See proposals file.
'Zokubutsu' (vulgar, worldly person) rendered 'Philistine'. Muttered by the rebuked officer about the captain; speaker untagged.

Fragment 'to/by a former Vulture...' with the verb cut off. Context (1685-1688) suggests Jurgens resenting help or a lecture from Shagia, but the omitted verb is unknown; rendered 'From a Vulture upstart...'. Calling the Frost brothers ex-Vultures is ACE3's own setting, not Gundam X canon.
'Izumo-kan' could be the captain addressing his own ship/crew ('Izumo, prepare to withdraw') or a statement that the Izumo will prepare to withdraw. Read as an order to the ship.
Number of Dewey's subordinates aboard is unmarked in Japanese; 'one of' chosen because 1678-1679 show a single intelligence officer (Dominic). Alternative: 'Dewey's people should be on that ship.'

1711 quotes the Eureka Seven motto; the official English dub wording is used ('Don't beg for things. Do it yourself, or else you won't get anything'). The Japanese literally says 'Don't beg, win it, and then it shall be given', so the dub inverts the last clause. 1698-1700 paraphrase the motto and are translated literally ('Begging won't do / I'm going out to win it myself'). Reviewer may prefer the literal motto: 'Don't beg for it. Earn it, and it shall be given... huh.'
Drawn-out English 'I can fly' in kana; rendered as stretched English. Avoids lowercase j/q.

Literally 'my younger brother was in your care the other day' (sarcastic courtesy before a fight). 'The other day' implies an earlier meeting with the younger brother; rows 261+ may belong to a later/alternate encounter than rows 131-137.
Object ('that kid', 1709) omitted in source; passive used. 1696 calls the kid Adroc's son, so 'him' would also be supported.
Enemy ace lines using formal first person, read as the elder Frost brother answering 1714 (YF-19 charge) and taunting the GX pilot; untagged, no names added.
Plain-form declaration 'will destroy all targets' with no subject; imperative used to avoid inventing 'I/we'.

<on()> event-scene lines (text ids 301-321) are stored in table order; several are bare interjections with no settled speaker. 1725's subject is omitted ('must link up with Holland soon'); kept subjectless.
'Ending at 14 years' = the speaker's age; rendered 'over after 14 years'.
